A producer plans to add ₹1,20,000 to inventory by the end of the year. To meet extra demand, she later sells goods worth ₹35,000 from that inventory. Assume no other changes to inventory occur. Arrange the following events and steps in the order that leads from the producer’s plan to identifying actual investment.
(A) The producer plans an addition of ₹1,20,000 to inventory.
(B) The producer sells ₹35,000 worth of goods from inventory to meet extra demand.
(C) The net increase in inventory is calculated as ₹1,20,000 − ₹35,000 = ₹85,000.
(D) The amount of ₹85,000 is identified as actual (ex post) investment.
Choose the correct sequence:
A. (A)-(C)-(B)-(D)
B. (B)-(A)-(C)-(D)
C. (A)-(B)-(C)-(D)
D. (A)-(B)-(D)-(C)
before.explanation: The planned addition is ₹1,20,000, and the later sale from inventory reduces the net increase by ₹35,000. Thus, actual investment is ₹1,20,000 − ₹35,000 = ₹85,000. The plan and sale must be accounted for before calculating and identifying the actual investment.
